_README: STAGE 1 RE-MEASUREMENT under TESTBENCH_PROMPT_VERSION 3 (the DIALECT + CONCURRENCY rules).
A true A/B against .eval-runs/stage1-screen-v2: identical arms (all 11 catalog models),
identical 15 designs, identical n=3, identical caps/limits/seed/temperature. The ONLY
difference is the two new Testbench_Agent prompt rules, so a change in instrument-valid
rate or in the did-not-build count is attributable to them.
The two numbers this run exists to move, per arm:
did-not-build      -> the DIALECT rule. Baseline 25% of 322 invalid samples; worst arms
qwen3-235b 27, qwen3-coder-30b 17, qwen3-coder-480b 13.
rejected-reference -> the CONCURRENCY rule. Baseline ~60%. This is the THIRD attempt at
this class; the two prior prompt attempts both looked right and
both failed on re-measurement, so treat any improvement here as
provisional until it holds on a second slice.
Baseline instrument-valid, for reference: glm-4.7 6/38, glm-5 6/39, kimi 5/38,
deepseek 3/39, qwen3-coder-480b 3/42, qwen3-235b 2/41, devstral 2/38,
qwen3-coder-next 1/32, qwen3-coder-30b 0/34, mistral-large 0/2, minimax 3/13.
All 11 arms are kept even though 6 were screened out for RTL capability: the dialect fix
is most visible on the arms with the WORST baseline, and two of those (qwen3-235b,
qwen3-coder-30b) are in the dropped set. Measuring the fix and picking the shipping model
are different questions.
THE CREDENTIAL NEVER GOES IN THIS FILE. AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK comes from .env.
_problems: The same 15 designs as sweep.config.tbslice.json, spanning arithmetic, control, memory,
and miscellaneous, none of them Stage 0 quarantined. Reused deliberately: we already
have a kimi-k2.5 reading on this exact set (tbslice-v2), so that arm doubles as a
sanity check that this screen reproduces a known result.
_caps: The SAME student-session caps a real student gets. Never widened for eval.
_concurrency: 3, not 1. The two previous wide attempts (instrument-calibration, stage1-screening) both
died to a rate-limit burst, so this stays well under the host limit while still cutting
a ~2h serial run to well under an hour. The breaker and backoff handle the rest.
_killSwitch: 6h wall and 550 samples: 495 planned (11 arms x 15 problems x 3) plus headroom. Stops
DISPATCH at a sample boundary, so everything recorded stays on disk and resumable.
_sampling: n=3, NOT n=1, and this was measured rather than assumed.
stage1-screen-v1 ran this same config at n=1 and was ABANDONED after 15 samples, because
the kimi-k2.5 arm disagreed with the tbslice-v2 run on 3 of its first 10 problems - all
three flipping verified -> instrument-refused on identical inputs at temperature 0.
The artifacts name the cause: instrument_control_tb.v syntax errors / Malformed statement,
i.e. the MODEL emitted different, invalid testbench Verilog on the second run. Not a
timeout, not sandbox contention - a genuinely stochastic generator. temperature 0 and a
fixed seed are hints to a hosted endpoint, never a guarantee.
So n=1 cannot rank models: a model could place last on variance alone. n=3 gives pass@1
and pass@3 plus a per-arm spread to read the noise floor off. .eval-runs/stage1-screen-v1
is kept as the evidence for this choice.
